The '''2026–27 season''' is [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|123rd season in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|96th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2026–27 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid is participating in this season's editions of the [[2026–27 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2027 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

This season is the first since [[2012–13 Real Madrid CF season|2012–13]] without youth graduate and captain [[Dani Carvajal]], as well as the first since [[2020–21 Real Madrid CF season|2020–21]] without [[David Alaba]], both of whom departed as free agents, to [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]], respectively.<ref name=":1"/><ref name=":0"/>

The departure of Carvajal marked the end of the club's association with the last remaining player from the squad that won the UEFA Champions League in three consecutive seasons, in [[2016 UEFA Champions League final|2016]], [[2017 UEFA Champions League final|2017]] and [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018]] respectively.

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
On 18 May 2026, Madrid announced an agreement with [[Dani Carvajal]] for the club captain to depart after 23 seasons within the club's ranks. He left as the holder of 27 senior trophies and as one of only five players in football history to [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Most wins|have won six European Cups]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Guillermo|first=Rai|last2=Cortegana|first2=Mario|title=Real Madrid announce captain Dani Carvajal will leave club this summer|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7248059/2026/05/16/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-transfer/|publisher=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|work=The Athletic|date=18 May 2026|access-date=22 May 2026|archive-date=20 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260520012102/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7248059/2026/05/16/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-transfer/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 May, the club confirmed the departure of [[David Alaba]], who concluded his five-year spell at Real Madrid with eleven trophies, including two UEFA Champions League titles.<ref>{{cite web|last=Guillermo|first=Rai|last2=Millar|first2=Colin|title=David Alaba to leave Real Madrid at end of season|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6522112/2026/05/22/david-alaba-real-madrid-transfer/|publisher=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|work=The Athletic|date=22 May 2026|access-date=22 May 2026|archive-date=22 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260522175707/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6522112/2026/05/22/david-alaba-real-madrid-transfer/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 June, following the first presidential vote by club members in two decades, [[Florentino Pérez]] was elected president in the extraordinary elections announced on 12 May.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official statement from the Electoral Board: the candidacy of Florentino Pérez wins the elections for President and Board of Directors of Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-de-la-junta-electoral-resultado-elecciones-07-06-2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=7 June 2026|access-date=8 June 2026|archive-date=8 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260608005013/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-de-la-junta-electoral-resultado-elecciones-07-06-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 June, Madrid reached an agreement with [[Álvaro Arbeloa]] to end his tenure as first-team head coach.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Statement: Arbeloa|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-arbeloa-09-06-2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=9 June 2026|access-date=9 June 2026|archive-date=9 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260609182224/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-arbeloa-09-06-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 June, [[José Mourinho]] returned as the club's head coach, signing a contract running until 30 June 2029, effective from 13 July.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: José Mourinho|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-mourinho-11-06-2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=11 June 2026|access-date=11 June 2026|archive-date=12 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260612110907/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-mourinho-11-06-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Madrid's first summer signing was confirmed on 15 June, when [[Marc Cucurella]] joined from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on a six-year contract, with the move set to become effective after the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ornstein|first=David|title=Real Madrid complete €60m Marc Cucurella signing from Chelsea|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7325256/2026/06/14/marc-cucurella-real-madrid-chelsea-transfer/|publisher=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|work=The Athletic|date=15 June [[Antonio Rüdiger]] committed his future to the club by signing a one-year contract extension until 2027.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Antonio Rüdiger signs one-year Real Madrid contract extension|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7309304/2026/05/26/antonio-rudiger-real-madrid-future/|publisher=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|work=The Athletic|date=16 June the signing of [[Bernardo Silva]] on a free transfer from [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], with the Portuguese midfielder agreeing a two-year contract after the World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|last=Guillermo|first=Rai|title=Bernardo Silva joins Real Madrid on two-year contract|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7353853/2026/06/17/bernardo-silva-real-madrid-transfers/|publisher=The New Konaté]] also arrived on a free transfer, leaving [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to sign a four-year deal with the club.<ref>{{cite web|last=Millar|first=Colin|last2=Guillermo|first2=Rai|title=Ibrahima Konaté joins Real Madrid on four-year deal after Liverpool exit|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7372321/2026/06/18/konate-real-madrid-transfers-liverpool/|publisher=The New York 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260618093723/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7372321/2026/06/18/konate-real-madrid-transfers-liverpool/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 June, [[Dani Ceballos]] departed the club after his contract was terminated by mutual consent, bringing an end to a nine-year association during which he collected fifteen trophies.<ref>{{cite exit|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/ceballos-announces-his-real-madrid-exit-2026-06-26/|publisher=Reuters|date=26 June 2026|access-date=27 June 2026|archive-date=27 June García|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-fran-garcia-08-07-2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 July 2026|access-date=8 July 2026|archive-date=8 July ===August===
On 22 August, Madrid opened the new campaign with a 2–1 victory away at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], as [[Carlos Espí]] scored a late close-range winner after [[Jude Bellingham]] had also found the net.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Debutant Espí gives Mourinho winning Real Madrid return|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmwyjzndv4xnt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 August 2026|access-date=22 August 2026|archive-date=23 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823180042/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmwyjzndv4xnt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, [[Kylian Mbappé]] recorded his first goals of the season by scoring a hat-trick, while Vinícius added another goal as Madrid secured a 4–1 win over [[Real Sociedad]] at the [[Bernabéu (stadium)|Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Gary|title=Mourinho says hat-trick hero Mbappé 'hungry' for Real Madrid history|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck24mej548lvt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 August 2026|access-date=27 August 2026|archive-date=27 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260827073823/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck24mej548lvt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 August, Madrid beat [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] 4–0 at home to maintain their perfect start to the league campaign, with Bellingham, Mbappé and [[Arda Güler]] all finding the net alongside an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Málaga: Jude Bellingham scores as José Mourinho's Real win again in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmvgyx9y35n8t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=30 August 2026|access-date=30 August 2026|archive-date=30 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830181438/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmvgyx9y35n8t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===September===
Madrid suffered their first defeat of the season on 4 September, losing 1–0 to Real Betis in the league.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Betis 1–0 Real Madrid: Substitute Troy Parrott scores winner as José Mourinho suffers first loss|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3n071elp7jyt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 September 2026|access-date=4 September 2026|archive-date=4 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260904213907/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3n071elp7jyt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 September, Madrid beat [[Inter Milan]] 2–1 in their Champions League opener, with goals from Mbappé and [[Federico Valverde]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Inter Milan: Mbappé & Valverde score as Real win opener|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm7903l5470dt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 September 2026|access-date=8 September 2026|archive-date=9 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260909133934/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm7903l5470dt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid beat [[Rayo Vallecano]] 4–1 at home, with Mbappé scoring twice and [[Álvaro Carreras]] and Bellingham also finding the net.<ref>{{cite web|last=MacDonald|first=Keifer|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Rayo Vallecano: Kylian Mbappé shines as Real Madrid thrash Rayo Vallecano|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr1e50y62d1dt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=12 September 2026|access-date=12 September 2026|archive-date=12 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260912213424/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr1e50y62d1dt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 September, Madrid defeated [[Elche CF|Elche]] 3–2 away from home, with Mbappé and an own goal giving Madrid a two-goal lead before Espí scored the stoppage-time winner after Elche had fought back to level.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Barlow|first1=Ruairidh|last2=Davis|first2=Toby|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/espi-winner-rescues-real-madrid-after-elche-comeback-2026-09-15/|title=Espí winner rescues Real Madrid after Elche comeback|publisher=Reuters|date=15 September 2026|access-date=16 September 2026|archive-date=16 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260916163601/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/espi-winner-rescues-real-madrid-after-elche-comeback-2026-09-15/|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Real lost 1–2 to [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[Madrid derby]], with Rüdiger scoring the only goal for the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Atlético Madrid 2–1 Real Madrid: José Mourinho's men beaten in feisty derby|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c61mv7p2k4dlt|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2026|access-date=20 September 2026|archive-date=20 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260920173649/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c61mv7p2k4dlt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
Following a lengthy [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], Madrid returned to action on 10 October in their first match of the month, defeating [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 1–0 at the Bernabéu, with Diomande scoring his first goal for the club in the second half to secure the victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Villarreal: Vinícius Jr sent off for hair pull in win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx30eppd991et|publisher=BBC Sport|date=10 October 2026|access-date=11 October 2026|archive-date=11 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011113723/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx30eppd991et|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid staged a comeback from 1–3 down to win 4–3 away from home against [[AS Roma|Roma]] in the Champions League, completing the turnaround in the final ten minutes with goals from Mbappé, Espí, [[Endrick]] and Rüdiger.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emmons|first=Michael|title=Roma 3–4 Real Madrid: Los Blancos win after stunning late fightback|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmwyqp5q1lypt|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 October 2026|access-date=14 October 2026|archive-date=14 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261014222637/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cmwyqp5q1lypt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 October, Madrid secured a 4–1 win over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at home, with Güler opening the scoring before Mbappé struck twice and Diomande added a fourth to round off the victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Sevilla - Kylian Mbappé scores twice as Real win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cw0k0xyeee56t|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 October 2026|access-date=18 October 2026|archive-date=18 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018211633/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cw0k0xyeee56t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid defeated RB Leipzig 4–1 on matchday three of the Champions League league phase, maintaining their perfect record in the competition, as Silva opened his scoring account for the club before Güler, Mbappé and Diomande also found the net.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 4–1 RB Leipzig: Spanish side maintain 100% start|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5vgjnkyyxr7t|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 October 2026|access-date=21 October 2026|archive-date=21 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261021214114/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5vgjnkyyxr7t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 October, a brace from Mbappé sealed the win in the first [[El Clásico]] of the season, beating [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 2–1 at the [[Camp Nou|Spotify Camp Nou]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Cartwright|first=Phil|title=Barcelona 1–2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores twice to end La Liga leaders winning start|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3vqz410y42t|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 October 2026|access-date=25 October 2026|archive-date=25 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261025221718/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj3vqz410y42t|url-status=live}}</ref>
